destaque.titulo: COP31 ends without agreement due to dispute over fossil fuels
destaque.oQueAconteceu: The United Nations Conference of the Parties (COP31), held in Antalya, Turkey, concluded on 22 November 2026 without the adoption of a final agreement. The main cause was the divergence between country blocs over the inclusion of language that would require the gradual phase‑out of fossil fuels and over financing for the most vulnerable nations. About 200 countries participated, but the EU, Panama and other blocs rejected the proposed text because it did not contain an explicit reference to the phasing out of fossils. On the other hand, India, China and Saudi Arabia advocated maintaining less restrictive language. The deadlock marked the first time since Copenhagen 2009 that the COP failed to approve a final declaration, prompting calls to reform the consensus requirement and to seek parallel agreements among groups of countries with similar positions.

The inability to reach an agreement jeopardizes the global pace of emission reductions and the flow of financial resources destined for developing countries. For Brazil, this could mean delays in the release of international funds that support clean energy and climate adaptation projects, strategic areas for the country's energy transition.

Moreover, the split between blocs highlights the difficulty of aligning climate policies with economic interests, which could influence bilateral and multilateral negotiations in which Brazil participates, such as the Paris Agreement and regional forums in Latin America.
